description: A whole-degree tour of what a computer is, how information is represented and moved, and what computing does to society, so that every later course has a map to hang on. Taught to the depth of a leading introductory computer science survey, with hands-on exercises for every idea.
modelledOn: Brookshear and Brylow, Computer Science: An Overview
Schneider and Gersting, Invitation to Computer Science
Petzold, Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
outcomes: Describe the parts of a computer and trace how a program and its data move from storage to processor and back.
Represent text, numbers, images and sound in binary and estimate storage and bandwidth needs.
Explain what algorithms, programs, operating systems and compilers are and how they fit together.
Organise information in files, spreadsheets and relational databases and query it.
Explain how the Internet and the Web work end to end, from a URL to a rendered page.
Reason about safety, privacy, ethics and the social impact of computing with Ghanaian and global examples.

units.title: What computing is
topics: History of computing: from the abacus and Babbage to the transistor, the microprocessor and the smartphone
Computational thinking: decomposition, abstraction, patterns, algorithms
Hardware, software, data and people as the parts of a computing system
Kinds of computers: embedded, mobile, personal, server, supercomputer, cloud

units.title: Representing information
topics: Bits and bytes; binary, hexadecimal; units from kilobyte to petabyte
Integers and two's complement; floating point and why 0.1 + 0.2 is not 0.3
Text: ASCII, Unicode and UTF-8; representing Twi and other Ghanaian languages
Images (pixels, colour depth, compression), sound (sampling, bit depth) and video
Compression: run-length, Huffman and the difference between lossless and lossy
Error detection: parity and checksums

units.title: Inside the computer
topics: Logic gates and how they add; the processor, registers, clock and the fetch-decode-execute cycle
Memory hierarchy: registers, cache, RAM, SSD, hard disk, cloud storage
Input and output devices, buses and ports
Machine code, assembly, high-level languages, compilers and interpreters
Operating systems: what they do for programs and users; processes and files

units.title: Algorithms and programs
topics: Algorithms as precise procedures; pseudocode and flowcharts
Sequence, selection and iteration; variables and data types
Searching and sorting by hand: linear search, binary search, bubble and selection sort
Why some algorithms are faster: counting steps, growth with input size
Writing and running short programs in Scratch and Python to see the ideas work
Software: system software, application software, open source, licences

units.title: Information management, files and databases
topics: Data, information and knowledge; data quality and data life cycle
File systems, folders, file formats, metadata; backup and archiving
Spreadsheets for data: formulas, sorting, filtering, charts
Relational databases: tables, keys, relationships; simple SQL SELECT queries
Database applications: student records, mobile money ledgers, hospital systems
Big data and data centres: what changes at scale

units.title: Computer networks, the Internet and the Web
topics: LANs, WANs, Wi-Fi, mobile data; switches and routers
IP addresses, DNS, packets and the layered model in plain terms
What happens when you type a URL: HTTP, HTML, CSS, JavaScript, servers and browsers
Email, cloud services, content delivery and why pages load slowly on poor links
Submarine cables and Ghana's connectivity; data costs and digital inclusion
Building a one-page website

units.title: Computer safety, security and ethics
topics: Threats: malware, phishing, mobile money scams, social engineering
Passwords, two-factor authentication, encryption and HTTPS in plain terms
Personal data, privacy and Ghana's Data Protection Act
Professional ethics and the ACM Code; plagiarism and academic integrity
Safe and healthy computer use

units.title: Technology and society
topics: Computing in Ghana and Africa: mobile money, agritech, e-government, health informatics
Automation, AI and the future of work; the digital divide
Environmental cost of computing: energy, e-waste at Agbogbloshie
Careers and the map of the computer science degree ahead

schedule.title: What computing is
schedule.exercise: Make a one-page timeline of five computing milestones and decompose an everyday task, such as buying airtime, into steps a computer could follow.

tasks.title: Identify the hardware parts of a desktop PC in the assembly bench and sort them into input, processing, storage and output
Choose between a microcontroller board, a single-board computer and a PC for three given jobs and justify each choice by cost and power
Decompose the problem of giving change in cedis into steps, write it as a Python function and test it on 10 amounts

schedule.title: Numbers and text in binary
schedule.exercise: Convert six numbers between decimal, binary and hexadecimal by hand, then write the UTF-8 bytes of a short Twi word.

tasks.title: Convert 10 decimal values to binary and hex with the base converter and check each by converting back
Print 0.1 + 0.2 in Python, show its binary floating-point value and encode -37 as 8-bit two's complement, verifying by adding 37
Encode a Twi sentence in UTF-8, count bytes per character, then show what garbled text appears when it is decoded as Latin-1

schedule.title: Media, compression and error detection
schedule.exercise: Compute the size of one minute of CD-quality stereo audio and a 10 megapixel photo, then explain what lossy compression discards.

tasks.title: Apply run-length encoding to five short strings and a small pixel row and compute the compression ratio of each
Add an even-parity bit to 10 bytes, flip one bit in three of them and show which corruptions the parity check detects
Build the Huffman tree for a 40-character message, assign codes, encode the message and compare its length with fixed 8-bit codes

schedule.title: Inside the computer
schedule.exercise: Draw a half adder and full adder from gates, then describe what happens in each step of one fetch-decode-execute cycle.

tasks.title: Build a half adder from XOR and AND gates and verify all four input cases in the truth table
Step a tiny CPU through a 5-instruction program, recording the program counter and register values after each fetch-decode-execute cycle
Run a memory access sequence through a small cache, count hits and misses, and change the cache size to see the effect on average access time

schedule.title: Programs and operating systems
schedule.exercise: Compare compiling and interpreting using one small program, and list five jobs an operating system does when you open a file.

tasks.title: Trace a short assembly program that adds two numbers, listing the machine instruction behind each line and the final register values
List running processes in the terminal, start and stop a background job and report its process ID and state at each step
Create a folder tree for a school project, set file permissions so only the owner can edit, and verify access as another user

schedule.title: Algorithms and basic programming
schedule.exercise: Write pseudocode and a flowchart for finding the highest mark in a class list and trace it with five marks.

tasks.title: Write a Python program using a loop and an if statement to total only the marks above 50 in a list of 10 scores
Run linear and binary search on a sorted list of 16 numbers for three targets and compare the number of comparisons
Compare bubble sort and selection sort on three 10-element lists and record the swaps and comparisons for each

schedule.title: Efficiency and software
schedule.exercise: Count the steps for linear and binary search on lists of 8, 1000 and 1 million items, and compare open source and proprietary licences for a school.

tasks.title: Write a Python program that asks for a number and prints its multiplication table, then test it with 3 inputs
Time linear search and binary search on lists of 1000, 100000 and 1 million items and plot how the time grows
Plot step counts for n, n squared and 2 to the n for n up to 30 and decide which algorithms stay usable at one million inputs

schedule.title: Data, files and spreadsheets
schedule.exercise: Design a file naming and folder scheme with a backup plan for a small shop's records, and list three data quality problems in a messy sheet.

tasks.title: Create, copy, rename and delete files in the terminal, then list file sizes and modification times for a folder of five documents
Enter 20 rows of shop sales, compute totals with formulas, sort by amount and filter to one product, then chart the monthly totals
Clean a CSV of 30 survey rows with duplicates, blanks and mixed date formats and report how many records each fix changed

schedule.title: Databases and big data
schedule.exercise: Draw the tables for a mobile money ledger with their primary and foreign keys, and write down three questions it should answer.

tasks.title: Write SELECT queries to list all students, those in one class and those sorted by mark from a given student table
Query a mobile money ledger for total deposits per customer and the five largest transactions, checking totals against the sample data
Design customer, account and transaction tables with keys for a hospital clinic, insert sample rows and join them to answer two questions

schedule.title: Networks and the web
schedule.exercise: Describe step by step what happens between typing a URL on your phone and the page appearing, naming DNS, IP and HTTP.

tasks.title: Connect four PCs to a switch and a router in the simulator, assign IP addresses and ping between every pair
Send a packet across two routers, inspect the headers at each hop and note how the addresses change or stay the same
Set up a web server and DNS name on the simulated network and fetch the page from a client, then break DNS and diagnose it

schedule.title: The internet in Ghana and your first website
schedule.exercise: Estimate how much a 3 MB web page costs on a prepaid data bundle and suggest three changes that would cut that cost.

tasks.title: Write a one-page website with a heading, paragraph, image and link in HTML and check it renders correctly in the preview
Style a one-page site with CSS for mobile screens and add a short JavaScript button that changes the greeting text
Compare page load times over a fast link and a slow high-latency link in the simulator and list changes that help the slow user

schedule.title: Security, privacy and ethics
schedule.exercise: Write guidance for a relative on spotting a mobile money scam, and list what personal data a shop may lawfully collect.

tasks.title: Estimate how long it takes to guess passwords of 6, 8 and 12 characters with different alphabets and compare the numbers
Work through a mobile money scam case, choose responses at each decision point and review your score against the rubric
Decide how a small clinic should handle a patient data request and a plagiarism case under the data protection law and academic rules

schedule.title: Computing in society and what comes next
schedule.exercise: Write a short essay on how one computing technology has changed life in Ghana and one risk it creates, then plan your own degree path.

tasks.title: Explore a career-choice scenario, pick learning steps for three roles and read the feedback on each choice's skill gaps
Estimate the yearly energy use and carbon footprint of 100 office PCs and compare with replacing them using a spreadsheet model
Debate automation of a cashier or clerk role in a branching case, weigh jobs, cost and access, and justify a decision against the rubric
